messages.author: 4140d98df209a83d
messages.subject: borderline of the mask area
parts:
Hi Group, I wold like to know how to plot only the borderline of the mask area.

I am using the white color to avoid too much information in the figure but I lost the information of the effectively sampled area.


> Habitat <- make.mask(traps(ocelot1.data),  type = "trapbuffer", buffer = 4734,  poly = Classes)
> oldpar <-par(mar=c(1,6,6,6), xpd = TRUE)
> HabitatMask2 <- addCovariates(Habitat, Classes)
> plot(HabitatMask2, ppoly=TRUE, col="white", pch=3)

Anyone could help me?

Thanks,

Cristiano

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: borderline of the mask area
parts:
Hi Cristiano
Did you find the function plotMaskEdge? That should do what you want. Or just plot Classes (perhaps after merging polygons with rgeos::gUnaryUnion).  I think you mis-spoke when you mentioned 'effectively sampled area' - the effective sampling area is not a geographic region that you can show on a map.
Regards
Murray

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: borderline of the mask area
parts:
Presumably the grey is from plot.mask - change the default colour if you don't like it.

The effective sampling area is the number that can be divided into the number of detected individuals to give an unbiased estimate of population density. It is not the masked area, and does not correspond to a mappable region..

Murray
